provenance.source: q-system/output/blocked-claim-lint.jsonl, the advisory log this hook writes, read from 14 fleet instances
provenance.sampling: per trigger, random.seed(459), a fixed sample of distinct finding texts; does-not-exist has a second 50-row sample; nothing-was-written is its whole population
provenance.label_rule: genuine = the sentence asserts, as present fact, a settleable state of something outside the author's current action (blocked, denied, unavailable, missing, nonexistent, live, never ran, nothing written). noise = past-event narration ('the hook blocked me'), dependency or tracker prose ('blocked on your call'), conditional or generic prose, an adjective ('the blocked PRs'), a description of code behaviour, a heading, table cell or quotation, or narration of a process the author just started ('the suite is running').
provenance.rows: the labelled sentences are NOT in this repo: they are fleet session prose and this repo is public. They live on the calibrating machine; set KIPI_BLOCKED_CLAIM_REPLAY to that file to run the drift and replay checks. This file carries counts only.
provenance.trigger_attribution: re-derived after the blocking-trigger-first fix; 1 row(s) moved trigger
